text.en: Dog owners praise Dean for his calm, rational, and non-judgemental coaching style during one-to-one sessions. Clients note that he listens carefully to their specific concerns and explains canine psychology in accessible terms. Reviewers frequently describe him as a supportive mentor who trains both dogs and their handlers.

Clients report that Dean quickly earns the trust of anxious, young, and dog-reactive pets using gentle reinforcement techniques. Owners of puppies and rescue dogs appreciate his structured guidance on managing canine impulses. Dogs visibly enjoy the training walks and build lasting confidence under his supervision.

Reviewers highlight rapid improvements in loose lead walking, reliable recall, and calm responses around other dogs. Owners report feeling significantly more confident managing their pets after only a few outdoor sessions. The practical exercises provide long-term behavioral benefits for household routines.

q.en: Where do training sessions typically take place?

a.en: Clients mention meeting on Hampstead Heath for outdoor sessions alongside initial home visits.

q.en: Does Dean Ashton help with reactive rescue dogs?

a.en: Yes, reviewers note effective techniques that helped manage intense leash reactivity in rescue dogs.

q.en: Does the training cover puppy fundamentals?

a.en: Yes, owners praise his tailored advice on puppy socialization, loose lead walking, and impulse control.

q.en: Is ongoing support provided between sessions?

a.en: Yes, clients appreciate that Dean offers follow-up exercises and remains contactable for guidance.
